display.name: Coregw — MVC / WebFlux · JVM & HTTP Operations
display.description: JVM template adapted to Micrometer: CPU, memory pools, GC, threads, class loading, HTTP. Select one instance for diagnosis. No-data is not zero/healthy. No agent JVM metrics are duplicated.

display.name: App scrape health
display.description: 1 = reachable, 0 = down. Read together with Sample age; scalar panels can retain the last value in the selected range. Synthetic up has no mode/environment tag.

display.name: Telemetry sample age
display.description: Age of the newest scrape sample per target, worst selected target. Investigate values above 20s at a 5s scrape interval. A stopped collector can otherwise leave stale scalar values visible.

display.name: Scrape target count
display.description: Targets represented by scrape health series; includes down targets. Check Sample age and do not interpret as healthy JVM count.

display.name: CPU usage · max
display.description: Fraction of CPU capacity visible to JVM. This is not percent of one core.

display.name: Heap utilization
display.description: Sum heap used per JVM divided by sum positive heap limits; ignores -1 undefined pool limits. Does not measure process RSS.

display.name: GC pause fraction
display.description: GC pause seconds per wall second, worst selected JVM; rate window applies.

display.name: HTTP requests/s
display.description: Total selected traffic, excludes actuator and benchmark prepare. Zero traffic is not an availability result.

display.name: HTTP p99 · max
display.description: Server-side histogram estimate. No requests/histogram means no percentile. End-to-end latency remains in k6.

display.name: HTTP throughput by JVM
display.description: Excludes scrape/prepare traffic. Grouped per instance and Redis mode.

display.name: HTTP 5xx ratio
display.description: HTTP 5xx / all business responses. A missing error series becomes zero only if a total series exists. Transport failures before the server are visible in k6, not here.

thresholds.label: Example: 1% errors; tune to your SLO

display.name: HTTP latency · p50 / p90 / p99
display.description: Percentiles from buckets, never average percentile values across JVMs. Each JVM is plotted separately.

spec.name: A
spec.query: label_replace((histogram_quantile(.5, sum by (le,"service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) (rate({__name__="http_server_requests_seconds.bucket","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",uri!~"/actuator.*|/api/bench/redis/prepare|UNKNOWN|NOT_FOUND"}[1m])))), "view", "p50", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((histogram_quantile(.9, sum by (le,"service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) (rate({__name__="http_server_requests_seconds.bucket","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",uri!~"/actuator.*|/api/bench/redis/prepare|UNKNOWN|NOT_FOUND"}[1m])))), "view", "p90", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((histogram_quantile(.99, sum by (le,"service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) (rate({__name__="http_server_requests_seconds.bucket","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",uri!~"/actuator.*|/api/bench/redis/prepare|UNKNOWN|NOT_FOUND"}[1m])))), "view", "p99", "__name__", ".*")

display.name: HTTP p99 by endpoint
display.description: Separate route/method series help identify the slow endpoint. A route with no samples has no percentile.

display.name: Tomcat threads · busy / current / max
display.description: Platform request workers by connector. Requires server.tomcat.mbeanregistry.enabled=true and application restart. Busy includes I/O wait, not just CPU work. Virtual-thread executors require separate interpretation.

display.name: Tomcat worker utilization · busy / max
display.description: Sustained near 100% indicates worker saturation. This is not queue length or queue wait time. Missing series is not zero.

display.name: Tomcat connections · current / keepalive / max
display.description: Open connections include idle keepalive; connections minus busy threads is not queue length.

display.name: WebFlux core connections · active / idle / max
display.description: WebFlux outbound core connection pool. No series under MVC is expected. Connections are not event-loop threads.

display.name: WebFlux core connections · pending / pending limit
display.description: Requests waiting to acquire an outbound core connection; not Tomcat worker queue length. No series under MVC is expected.

display.name: Process CPU vs host CPU
display.description: Both are capacity fractions; host includes Docker, SigNoz, k6 and other applications.

display.name: JVM CPU consumption · core equivalents
display.description: CPU nanoseconds/s divided by 1e9. 1.0 = one CPU core busy. This differs from process CPU capacity percent.

display.name: Available processors · minimum selected
display.description: Processors visible to JVM. Inspect one instance for exact capacity.

display.name: Uptime · youngest selected JVM
display.description: Low value shows a recent process restart; not host uptime.

display.name: Host 1-minute load / visible CPUs
display.description: Load average normalized by CPU count. 1.0 roughly means as many runnable entities as CPUs; not a CPU percentage.

display.name: Heap used / committed / max
display.description: Committed is JVM-owned capacity, max is its configured ceiling; neither is process RSS. Undefined per-pool limits are excluded.

spec.name: A
spec.query: label_replace((sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) ({__name__="jvm_memory_used_bytes","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",area="heap"})), "view", "used", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) ({__name__="jvm_memory_committed_bytes","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",area="heap"})), "view", "committed", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) ({__name__="jvm_memory_max_bytes","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",area="heap"} > 0)), "view", "max", "__name__", ".*")

display.name: Heap utilization & post-GC occupancy
display.description: Persistent high after-GC occupancy is more useful than transient Eden spikes. Values have different denominators; labels distinguish them.

spec.name: A
spec.query: label_replace(((sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) ({__name__="jvm_memory_used_bytes","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",area="heap"})) / (sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode) ({__name__="jvm_memory_max_bytes","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment",area="heap"} > 0))), "view", "heap used/max", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace(({__name__="jvm_memory_usage_after_gc","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment"}), "view", "after-GC long-lived occupancy", "__name__", ".*")

display.name: Heap pools · Old / Eden / Survivor
display.description: Actual pool names come from the running collector. G1 exposes Old Gen, Eden, Survivor; other collectors have different pools.

display.name: Non-heap pools · Metaspace / code / classes
display.description: Metaspace, compressed class space and code cache. Not heap and not total process RSS.

display.name: Direct / mapped buffer memory
display.description: JVM buffer-pool accounting; does not include all native allocations.

display.name: Direct / mapped buffer count
display.description: Buffer counts should be read alongside bytes. Idle stable buffers are not a leak.

display.name: Process resident memory · RSS
display.description: Darwin proc_pidinfo resident bytes, includes resident heap and native memory. Not equal to NMT committed. Native exporter follows MVC or WebFlux on port 8080 and labels process_pid.

display.name: Process context switches / second
display.description: Darwin process context switches, all native threads; not only Tomcat. Does not measure time spent switching. Counter is 32-bit on macOS and can wrap; rate handles resets.

display.name: Native thread stacks · reserved / committed
display.description: Requires JVM -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary at startup. Reserved is address space, committed is JVM accounting, neither is RSS. NMT sampled every 30s. Includes JVM native threads, not only Tomcat; not virtual-thread heap stacks.

display.name: NMT Thread category · reserved / committed
display.description: NMT Thread category includes stacks and thread bookkeeping. It is a superset of stack bytes: do not add them.

display.name: Native metrics · target / NMT available
display.description: Target=1 means matching MVC/WebFlux JVM discovered; NMT=0 means disabled or last sample failed, not zero native memory. Exporter must be running on host port 9257.

display.name: Native memory sample age
display.description: NMT polls every 30s; absent when unavailable. Native exporter does not invoke jcmd on the HTTP scrape thread.

display.name: Heap allocation / promotion rate
display.description: Counters update around GC. Short intervals can look bursty; use the same rate window for both benchmark modes.

display.name: GC pause fraction
display.description: Total pause time per second; shows impact rather than only event duration. Does not represent concurrent GC CPU.

display.name: GC events by collector / cause
display.description: Collection events/s grouped by JVM GC labels. Major/minor interpretation depends on the collector.

display.name: GC pauses · mean / p90 / p99
display.description: GC histogram requires app restart after jvm.gc.pause histogram is enabled. Until then only mean exists. No GC in the chosen window means no duration, not 0 ms.

spec.name: A
spec.query: label_replace((sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode,gc) (rate({__name__="jvm_gc_pause_seconds.sum","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment"}[1m])) / sum by ("service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode,gc) (rate({__name__="jvm_gc_pause_seconds.count","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment"}[1m]))), "view", "mean", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((histogram_quantile(.9, sum by (le,"service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode,gc) (rate({__name__="jvm_gc_pause_seconds.bucket","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment"}[1m])))), "view", "p90", "__name__", ".*") or label_replace((histogram_quantile(.99, sum by (le,"service.name","service.instance.id",redis_mode,gc) (rate({__name__="jvm_gc_pause_seconds.bucket","service.name"=~"$service","service.instance.id"=~"$instance",redis_mode=~"$mode",environment=~"$environment"}[1m])))), "view", "p99", "__name__", ".*")

display.name: JVM platform thread states
display.description: Runnable, waiting, timed-waiting, blocked, new, terminated. JVM MXBean thread metrics do not enumerate all Java virtual threads.

display.name: Platform threads · live / daemon / peak
display.description: Live includes daemon and non-daemon threads; daemon is a subset, never add the two. Peak is since process start/reset.

display.name: Classes currently loaded
display.description: Current class count; compare against Metaspace trend. This is not cumulative classes ever loaded.

display.name: Class loading / unloading rate
display.description: Counts/s, useful for class-loader churn. Interpret startup separately from steady state.

display.name: File descriptors · open / limit
display.description: Unix descriptor accounting. Includes sockets and files; it is not the Redis connection count.

display.name: JIT compilation time per second
display.description: Compiler milliseconds/s converted to seconds/s; helps identify JVM warm-up activity. Not CPU core utilization.
